At Porvoo, in March 1809, Tsar Alexander I of Russia met the Estates of Finland and promised to keep their laws, religion and rights. Finland became an autonomous grand duchy of the Russian Empire.

Russia had conquered Finland from Sweden in the Finnish War of 1808 to 1809. Rather than absorb it, the tsar gave it its own government, the Senate, its own currency later and its own customs. Helsinki became the capital in 1812.

For the first time Finland was a state of its own, not just the eastern half of Sweden. The Grand Duchy grew its own institutions and national culture, from the Kalevala to Sibelius. When Russia tried to curb its autonomy after 1899, the stage was set for independence in 1917. See Finland.
sum: At Porvoo, in March 1809, Tsar Alexander I of Russia met the Estates of Finland and promised to keep their laws, religion and rights. Finland became an autonomous grand duchy of the Russian Empire.
